mainTopic: Telling a group to write or deliver a גט, the start of the chapter on a husband seized by קורדייקוס, and the remedies and stories that follow.
overview: This amud starts by closing an earlier argument, noting that some switch the opinions of רבה and רב יוסף. Then a ברייתא explains what happens when a husband tells ten people to write or deliver a גט. A plain instruction lets one person act for all, but 'all of you' means everyone must be present. רב הונא and רבי יוחנן seem to argue about a husband who lists the people by name, and רב פפא explains that they are talking about different cases. רב יהודה offers a safe formula for speaking to a group, and רבא improves it by dropping 'all of you' completely. After the הדרן, a new chapter opens with a משנה about a husband seized by קורדייקוס and a mute husband who nods. The גמרא explains that קורדייקוס is confusion from new wine, named after a רוח. This leads into a list of remedies for fever and chills, and the story of how רב עמרם חסידא outsmarted the ריש גלותא's household. The amud ends with רב ששת proving that the ריש גלותא's servants are careless about אבר מן החי, and the story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Some people switch the two opinions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא closes the earlier discussion by noting that some people reverse which opinion belongs to רבה and which belongs to רב יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there are those who reverse them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the previous topic. It tells us that some people have a tradition where the two opinions of רבה and רב יוסף are swapped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added about the law itself. The only question is who said what. This line closes the previous סוגיא before a new topic begins.

phrases.english: And there are those who reverse them.
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the two opinions of רבה and רב יוסף from just before this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier dispute between רבה and רב יוסף from before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The attribution of the earlier opinions is reported both ways.

steps.title: A ברייתא on telling ten people to write or deliver a גט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of telling ten people 'write a גט' and brings a ברייתא. A plain instruction lets one act for all, while 'all of you' requires everyone to be present.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: If he said to ten people, 'Write a גט.' The Rabbis taught: If someone said to ten people, 'Write a גט and give it to my wife,' one of them writes on behalf of all of them. If he said, 'All of you write,' one writes while all of them are present. If he said, 'Deliver a גט to my wife,' one delivers on behalf of all of them. If he said, 'All of you deliver,' one delivers while all of them are present.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic by quoting the משנה's words. It brings a ברייתא that explains how the husband's exact wording changes what the ten people must do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a plain 'write' or 'deliver,' the husband just wants the job done, so any one of the ten can do it for all. Adding 'all of you' shows he wants the whole group involved. Even then only one person actually writes or carries the גט, but the rest must be standing there.

keyTerms.meaning: on behalf of all of them
in the presence of all of them

steps.whatToRemember: A plain instruction means one person can act for everyone. 'All of you' means one person acts, but everyone must be there.
steps.confusionAlert: Even when he says 'all of you write,' the ten do not each write a גט or write it together. One person writes it, and the others only need to be present.
steps.whyThisMatters: This basic rule is the background for the next question: what if he did not say 'all of you' but listed the people by name?

phrases.english: If he said to ten: 'Write a get.'
The Rabbis taught:
If one said to ten: 'Write a get and give it to my wife' –
one writes on behalf of them all.
'All of you write' –
one writes in the presence of them all.
'Deliver a get to my wife' –
one delivers on behalf of them all.
'All of you deliver' –
one delivers in the presence of them all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic based on the משנה, after the previous discussion was closed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A plain instruction lets one person act for all. 'All of you' requires one to act in the presence of all.

steps.title: What if he listed them by name?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether naming the people individually works like saying 'all of you.'
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: If he counted them out by name, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new question that the ברייתא did not answer. This sets up the opinions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא covered two kinds of wording: a plain instruction and 'all of you.' Listing names falls between them. Does naming each person show that he wants all of them involved, or not?

keyTerms.meaning: a question was asked among them

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
If he enumerated them, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a case in between the two kinds of wording in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether listing the people by name counts as saying 'all of you.'

steps.title: רב הונא: naming them is not like 'all of you'
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that listing names does not count as 'all of you,' so one person may act for all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא says: If he counted them by name, it is not like saying 'all of you.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question. Naming the people is treated like a plain instruction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב הונא's view, names alone do not show that the husband insists on everyone being present. So one person writes for all, just as in the ברייתא's first case.

phrases.english: Rav Huna says:
If he enumerated, it is not like 'all of you.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Listing names does not count as 'all of you.'

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: naming them is like 'all of you'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי אלעזר of Rome, rules the opposite: listing names counts as 'all of you.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says in the name of רבי אלעזר from Rome: If he counted them by name, it is like saying 'all of you.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion answers the same question the opposite way. Now it looks like רב הונא and רבי יוחנן disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this view, naming each person shows that the husband wants all of them involved. So one writes, but everyone must be present, like the ברייתא's 'all of you' case.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר דְּמִן רוֹמָה אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says in the name of Rabbi Elazar of Rome:
If he enumerated, it is like 'all of you.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר דְּמִן רוֹמָה אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite answer to רב הונא's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Listing names counts as 'all of you.'

steps.title: רב פפא: they are talking about different cases
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says there is no real disagreement. One opinion is about naming everyone, and the other is about naming only some. There are two versions of which opinion matches which case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: They do not disagree. This one is about where he named all of them, and that one is about where he named only some of them. Some say it one way, and some say it the other way.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא settles the apparent argument. Each opinion is about a different case, and he notes that there are two traditions about which opinion matches which case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Version one: naming all ten shows he wants everyone, so it is like 'all of you' (רבי יוחנן). Naming only some just tells us which people may do the job, so one can act for them (רב הונא). Version two: naming only some shows he wants those specific people involved, so it is like 'all of you' (רבי יוחנן). Naming all ten without saying 'all of you' is not like 'all of you' (רב הונא).
steps.whatToRemember: Naming the people is sometimes treated like 'all of you' and sometimes not. It depends on whether he named all of them or only some. There are two versions of which case is which.
steps.confusionAlert: The last line does not tell you which version is right. It only reports that the matching of opinions to cases goes both ways.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא method: two opinions that seem to clash are explained as talking about different cases.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
And they do not disagree;
this is where he enumerated all of them,
and that is where he enumerated some of them –
some say it this way,
phrases.notes: There are two versions of which opinion goes with naming all of them and which goes with naming only some.

phrases.english: and some say it that way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the apparent clash between steps 4 and 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each opinion applies to a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא and רבי יוחנן seemed to disagree about the same case of naming the people.
steps.terutzMaskana: One is about naming all of them and the other is about naming some of them, with two versions of which is which.

steps.title: רב יהודה's safe formula for instructing a group
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that a husband addressing a group should say 'either all of you or each one of you' for writing and delivering, and 'either all of you or every two of you' for signing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה made a rule for a גט where the husband might seem to be saying 'all of you.' He should say: Write it, either all of you or each one of you. Sign it, either all of you or every two of you. Deliver it, either all of you or each one of you.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives a set formula so that a husband speaking to many people does not accidentally require all of them to take part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From step 2 we know that saying 'all of you' means everyone must take part, so if one person does not, the גט is invalid. רב יהודה adds 'or each one' (or 'every two' for signing, because signing needs two witnesses). That way any one person, or any pair, may act. Saying 'all of you' as well also allows the whole group to act together.

keyTerms.meaning: He set up a rule (an enactment)
Each and every one of you
Deliver (bring the גט to the wife)

steps.whyThisMatters: It turns the theory from earlier steps into a practical rule, so the wording does not accidentally make a גט invalid.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda set up a rule for a bill of divorce involving 'all of you':

phrases.aramaic: כְּתוֹבוּ – אוֹ כּוּלְּכוֹן אוֹ כֹּל חַד וְחַד מִינְּכוֹן;
phrases.english: Write it: either all of you or each and every one of you;

phrases.aramaic: חֲתוֹמוּ – אוֹ כּוּלְּכוֹן אוֹ כֹּל תְּרֵי מִינְּכוֹן;
phrases.english: sign it: either all of you or every two of you;

phrases.aramaic: אוֹבִילוּ – אוֹ כּוּלְּכוֹן אוֹ כֹּל חַד וְחַד מִינְּכוֹן.
phrases.english: deliver it: either all of you or each and every one of you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining when wording counts as 'all of you,' a practical formula is given to avoid the problem.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The husband should say 'either all of you or each one (or every two) of you,' so the גט is valid even if not everyone takes part.

steps.title: רבא's worry that the husband will cut the formula short
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that a husband might say only 'all of you' and forget 'each one of you,' which would make the גט invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Sometimes a person cuts his words short. He says 'all of you' but does not say 'each one of you,' and the גט ends up invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב יהודה's formula. He says it is risky because people may not say all of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The danger is built into the formula, because it begins with 'all of you.' If the husband stops after those words, he has said exactly the phrase that requires everyone to take part. So the formula meant to protect the גט could end up making it invalid.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Sometimes he cuts his statement short,
and he says 'all of you' but does not say 'each one of you,'
and the bill of divorce will come to be invalid!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא זִימְנִין דְּגָאֵיז לֵיהּ לְדִיבּוּרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the practical safety of רב יהודה's formula.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's formula 'either all of you or each one of you'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Because the formula starts with 'all of you,' a husband who stops early has said only the dangerous phrase, which makes the גט invalid if one person does not take part.

steps.title: רבא's simpler formula without 'all of you'
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the husband should say only 'each one of you write, every two of you sign, each one of you deliver,' and leave out 'all of you' entirely.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said the husband should say: Each one of you write it, every two of you sign it, each one of you deliver it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא replaces רב יהודה's formula with a shorter one that never uses the risky words 'all of you.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אֶלָּא shows that רבא is setting aside the earlier formula. When 'all of you' is not in the formula at all, cutting it short can never leave only the dangerous phrase. The only words left allow any one person, or any pair for signing, to act.
steps.whatToRemember: The safe way to instruct a group: 'Each one of you write, every two of you sign, each one of you deliver.' Never say 'all of you,' because if even one person does not take part, the גט could be invalid.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
'Write it: each one of you;
sign it: every two of you;
deliver it: each one of you.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fixes the problem רבא raised in step 8 by changing the formula.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Saying 'either all of you or each one of you' covers every possibility.
steps.terutzMaskana: Leave out 'all of you' completely, so the husband cannot accidentally say only that phrase.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter הָאוֹמֵר
steps.stepSummary: The traditional closing line marking the end of the chapter הָאוֹמֵר.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter הָאוֹמֵר.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the chapter. It is not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Chapters are named after their opening words. הַדְרָן is a promise to come back and learn this chapter again. A new chapter begins after this line.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One who says,' the name of this chapter

phrases.english: We will return to you, chapter 'One Who Says'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after רבא's final formula.

steps.title: New chapter: a husband seized by confusion
steps.stepSummary: The new chapter's משנה rules that an order to write a גט given while seized by קורדייקוס is meaningless. A healthy order that he takes back while confused stays valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a man is seized by קורדייקוס and says 'Write a גט for my wife,' he has said nothing. If he said 'Write a גט for my wife' and then קורדייקוס seized him, and he went back and said 'Don't write it,' his last words mean nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter begins with a משנה about a husband who is temporarily not in his right mind. It explains which of his instructions about a גט count and which do not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט must be ordered by a husband with a clear mind. So an order given during the confusion has no effect. An order given while he was healthy is valid, and trying to cancel it while confused cannot undo it.

keyTerms.meaning: A temporary state of mental confusion
Seized him (the confusion took hold of him)
He said nothing, meaning his words have no legal effect

steps.confusionAlert: The two cases are mirror images. In both, what counts is what he said while his mind was clear. Words spoken during the confusion, whether to order the גט or to cancel it, mean nothing.

phrases.english: One who was seized by kordeyakos,
and said: "Write a bill of divorce for my wife"
has not said anything.
If he said: "Write a bill of divorce for my wife,"
and then kordeyakos seized him,
and he went back and said: "Do not write it"
his last words are nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new chapter right after the closing line of the previous chapter (Step 10).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An order or cancellation given during קורדייקוס has no effect. Only instructions given with a clear mind count.

steps.title: A mute husband who orders a divorce by nodding
steps.stepSummary: If the husband became mute and nods yes to writing a גט, he is tested three times. If his answers show a clear mind, the גט is written and given.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he became mute, and they said to him 'Shall we write a גט for your wife?' and he nodded his head, they test him three times. If he answers 'no' to questions whose answer is no, and 'yes' to questions whose answer is yes, they write the גט and give it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a husband who cannot speak. It explains how a nod can be enough to order a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A nod might be a random movement or a sign of confusion. So the court checks him with test questions three times. Correct answers prove the nod is a real, clear-minded answer.

keyTerms.meaning: He became mute and lost the ability to speak

steps.whatToRemember: A גט needs a husband with a clear mind. A confused husband's words don't count, while a mute husband can order a גט by nodding once tests show his mind is sound.

phrases.english: If he became mute,
and they said to him: "Shall we write a bill of divorce for your wife?"
and he nodded his head
they test him three times.
If to a 'no' question he answered "no,"
and to a 'yes' question he answered "yes,"
then these people may write and give it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second case to the משנה: a husband who cannot speak, in addition to one who is confused.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mute husband's nod counts as ordering a גט if he passes a test of three rounds of questions.

steps.title: What is קורדייקוס?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the unusual word קורדייקוס means.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is קורדייקוס?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking about the strange word in the משנה. This sets up שמואל's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the law can be understood, we need to know what condition the משנה is talking about. The word is not a regular Hebrew term, so the גמרא asks for a definition.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that analyzes the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is kordeyakos?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's analysis of the משנה's key term.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word קורדייקוס.

steps.title: שמואל: confusion caused by new wine
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that קורדייקוס is the state of someone overcome by new wine fresh from the winepress.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: It is one who was 'bitten' by new wine from the winepress.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question. קורדייקוס is the confusion that comes from drinking new wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: New wine straight from the press hits a person hard and can throw his mind into confusion. That passing state is what the משנה means.

keyTerms.meaning: That bit him, meaning it overcame him

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
One whom new wine has bitten
from the winepress.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: קורדייקוס is the confusion of someone overcome by new wine from the winepress.

steps.title: Why not just say 'new wine'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if this is about new wine, the משנה should have said so plainly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let the משנה teach: 'One who was bitten by new wine'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the wording of the משנה. If the cause is new wine, why use a strange word instead of just saying it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה usually uses clear words. Using an odd name where a simple phrase would work needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let it teach (why didn't the משנה say)

phrases.english: Then let it teach:
"One who was bitten by new wine"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's wording in light of שמואל's explanation.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's choice of the word קורדייקוס.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the condition is simply caused by new wine, the clearer wording 'new wine' should have been used.

steps.title: The name teaches us the spirit's name
steps.stepSummary: The משנה used the word קורדייקוס to teach that this is the name of the רוח (spirit) behind the condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches us that the name of this spirit is קורדייקוס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The strange word was used on purpose, to teach the name of the spirit that causes this confusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new wine is the trigger, but the condition is linked to a רוח named קורדייקוס. The משנה uses the name so we will know it.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it comes to teach us

phrases.english: This teaches us
that this spirit is named "kordeyakos."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains that the unusual wording adds information.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word קורדייקוס is just a needlessly unclear way of saying 'new wine.'
steps.terutzMaskana: The word teaches the name of the spirit behind the condition.

steps.title: Why does the name matter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference it makes to know the spirit's name.
steps.simpleTranslation: What practical difference does this make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we would need to know the spirit's name at all. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A detail is worth teaching only if it has some use. The גמרא wants to know what the use of this name is.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make?

phrases.english: What difference does it make?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the purpose of the answer given in Step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical use of knowing the spirit's name.

steps.title: For writing a קמיע
steps.stepSummary: Knowing the name matters for writing a קמיע (amulet) against this spirit.
steps.simpleTranslation: For an amulet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the name is needed for writing a קמיע, a protective amulet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An amulet against a spirit needs the spirit's name written in it. So the משנה's wording gives useful practical information.

keyTerms.meaning: An amulet worn for protection or healing

phrases.english: For an amulet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The name is needed for writing a protective amulet.

steps.title: What is the cure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the cure for קורדייקוס is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is its cure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a practical question: how is this condition treated? This sets up the remedy in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the condition has been identified, the גמרא turns from the law to medicine and asks how to heal it.

phrases.english: What is its cure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from defining the condition to asking how to treat it.

steps.title: Roasted red meat and diluted wine
steps.stepSummary: The cure is red meat roasted over coals and wine heavily diluted with water.
steps.simpleTranslation: Red meat over coals, and diluted wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the remedy: eat red meat roasted on coals and drink watered-down wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sick person was harmed by strong new wine. The cure gives him wine that is heavily diluted, together with roasted meat.
steps.whatToRemember: קורדייקוס is confusion from new wine. It carries the name of a רוח, which matters for a קמיע, and it is cured with roasted red meat and diluted wine.

phrases.english: Red meat roasted over coals,
and diluted wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Red meat roasted over coals and heavily diluted wine.

steps.title: אביי's remedies for a fever by how many days old it is
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes אם: a one-day fever needs a jug of water, a two-day fever needs bloodletting, and a three-day fever needs red meat over coals and diluted wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: My mother told me: For a fever one day old, a jug of water. Two days old, bloodletting. Three days old, red meat roasted over coals and diluted wine.
steps.whatsHappening: Right after the cure for קורדייקוס, אביי brings a list of fever remedies that changes depending on how long the fever has lasted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The treatment gets stronger the longer the fever lasts: first water, then bloodletting, then a special diet. The three-day cure is the same red meat and diluted wine just given for קורדייקוס in step 20.

phrases.english: Abaye said: My mother told me:
For a fever one day old —
a jug of water.
Two days old — bloodletting.
Three days old —
red meat roasted over coals,
and diluted wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the red meat and diluted wine cure from step 20 and places it inside a longer list of fever remedies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One-day fever: a jug of water. Two-day fever: bloodletting. Three-day fever: red meat over coals and diluted wine.

steps.title: The black hen remedy for a chronic fever
steps.stepSummary: For an old fever: tear a black hen lengthwise and widthwise, shave the middle of the sick person's head, and leave the hen on it until it sticks.
steps.simpleTranslation: For an old fever: let him bring a black hen, tear it lengthwise and widthwise, shave the middle of his head, place the hen on him, and leave it there until it sticks.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי's list continues to a fever that has lasted a long time. This step gives the first part of a longer cure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A chronic fever gets a much more involved treatment than the short fevers in step 21. This is only the first stage; the water stage comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Old, meaning a fever that has lasted a long time

phrases.english: For an old (chronic) fever —
let him bring a black hen,
and tear it lengthwise and widthwise,
and shave the middle of his head,
and place it (the hen) on him,
and leave it on him until it sticks;
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets is in the standard גמרא, but some versions word it differently.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's list, moving from short fevers to a chronic fever.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a chronic fever, a torn black hen is placed on the shaved middle of the head and left until it sticks.

steps.title: The water stage of the chronic fever cure
steps.stepSummary: The sick person stands in water up to his neck until he feels faint, dips under, then comes out and sits down.
steps.simpleTranslation: And let him go down and stand in water up to his neck until he feels faint. Then let him dip under, come up, and sit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the chronic fever cure with a second stage in the water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Standing in water until he feels faint is part of the same treatment that began with the hen. Afterward he dips under and then rests.

keyTerms.meaning: The world grows faint, meaning he feels weak and dizzy
Let him come up and sit

phrases.english: And let him go down and stand in the water up to his neck
until the world grows faint for him,
phrases.notes: He means until the person himself starts to feel faint.

phrases.english: and let him dip under, and come up and sit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second stage of the chronic fever cure that began in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the hen, he stands in water up to his neck until he feels faint, dips under, then comes out and rests.

steps.title: A backup cure using leeks
steps.stepSummary: If the first method isn't possible, he eats leeks and then does the same water treatment.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if not, let him eat leeks, then go down and stand in water up to his neck until he feels faint, dip under, come up, and sit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second option for someone who cannot do the first method. Leeks take the place of the first stage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The water stage is repeated word for word. Only the first part changes, from the hen to eating leeks.

phrases.english: And if not — let him eat leeks,
and let him go down and stand in the water up to his neck
until the world grows faint for him,
and let him dip under, and come up and sit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a backup to the hen method and repeats the same water stage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the first method isn't possible, eat leeks and then do the same water treatment.

steps.title: Fever and chills need opposite foods
steps.stepSummary: Fever: red meat over coals and diluted wine. Chills: fatty meat over coals and undiluted wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: For fever: red meat roasted over coals and diluted wine. For chills: fatty meat roasted over coals and undiluted wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets two cures side by side, one for fever and one for chills. This sets up the story that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cures mirror each other. Red meat goes with diluted wine for fever, and fatty meat goes with full-strength wine for chills. The story about רב עמרם depends on knowing this pair.
steps.whatToRemember: Fever is treated with red meat and diluted wine. Chills are treated with fatty meat and undiluted wine.

phrases.english: For fever — red meat roasted over coals,
and diluted wine.
For chills — fatty meat roasted over coals,
and undiluted wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the fever cure from step 21 next to its opposite, the cure for chills.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fever: red meat and diluted wine. Chills: fatty meat and undiluted wine.

steps.title: רב עמרם is made to lie on the snow
steps.stepSummary: The household of the ריש גלותא tormented רב עמרם חסידא by making him lie on snow, then asked him the next day what he would like them to bring.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the household of the ריש גלותא would torment רב עמרם the pious, they would make him lie on the snow. The next day they said to him: What would the Master like us to bring him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story that shows the fever and chills rules in action. This part sets the scene.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lying on snow would give רב עמרם chills, so he needs the chills cure from step 25. The question about what he wants to eat sets up his clever answer.

keyTerms.meaning: The Exilarch, leader of the Jews in Babylonia

phrases.english: Rav Amram the pious —

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲוָה מְצַעֲרִין לֵיהּ בֵּי רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא,
phrases.english: when the Exilarch's household would torment him,
they would make him lie on the snow.
The next day they said to him:
What would the Master like
for them to bring him?
phrases.notes: They speak politely about him as 'him', but they are really asking him directly.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב עַמְרָם חֲסִידָא, כִּי הֲוָה מְצַעֲרִין לֵיהּ בֵּי רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a story that illustrates the chills cure from step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב עמרם was given chills by the ריש גלותא's household and then asked what food he wanted.

steps.title: רב עמרם's reverse request gets him the right cure
steps.stepSummary: Knowing they always do the opposite, רב עמרם asked for the fever cure, and they brought him the chills cure, which is what he really needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to himself: These people do the opposite of anything I tell them. So he told them: Red meat over coals and diluted wine. They brought him fatty meat over coals and undiluted wine.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עמרם outsmarts his tormentors by asking for the opposite of what he needs. The story ends with him getting the right cure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He asked for the fever cure from step 25 on purpose. Because they did the opposite, he received the chills cure, which is exactly what someone who lay in the snow needs.
steps.whatToRemember: רב עמרם asked for the fever cure so his tormentors would bring the chills cure instead. This shows the two opposite cures from step 25 in action.

phrases.english: He said: These people, anything I tell them,
phrases.notes: He is thinking this to himself, not saying it to them.

phrases.english: they will surely do the opposite.
He said to them:
Red meat roasted over coals, and diluted wine.
They brought him:
Fatty meat roasted over coals, and undiluted wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר: הָנֵי, כֹּל דְּאָמֵינָא לְהוּ – מֵיפָךְ אָפְכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story begun in step 26 by showing how רב עמרם got the chills cure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By asking for the fever cure, רב עמרם received the chills cure he needed.

steps.title: ילתא treats רב עמרם in the bathhouse
steps.stepSummary: ילתא hears what happened to רב עמרם and takes him to the bathhouse. They keep him in the water until the water turns to blood and his skin breaks out in blotches.
steps.simpleTranslation: ילתא heard about it. She brought him into the bathhouse, and they stood him in the bathhouse water until the water turned into blood, and his skin broke out in blotches.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the story of רב עמרם חסידא. Someone who cared about him finally gives him the warming treatment he really needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the steps before, the household of the ריש גלותא had chilled רב עמרם by laying him in snow. Here ילתא has him stand in the bathhouse water until the water turns to blood and his skin breaks out in blotches. This shows how badly the cold had affected him.

keyTerms.meaning: the woman who rescued רב עמרם
patches upon patches; blotches on the skin

steps.whatToRemember: The רב עמרם story ends with ילתא healing him in the hot bathhouse, after the household of the ריש גלותא had made him sick.

phrases.english: Yalta heard
and she brought him into the bathhouse
and they stood him in the water of the bathhouse

phrases.aramaic: עַד דִּמְהַפְכִי מַיָּא דְּבֵי מַסּוּתָא וְהָווּ דְּמָא,
phrases.english: until the bathhouse water turned and became blood
and his flesh broke out in patches upon patches

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the רב עמרם story begun in steps 26-27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ילתא had רב עמרם kept in the bathhouse water until it turned to blood and his skin broke out in blotches.

steps.title: Hard work keeps you warm
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף kept warm by grinding at the millstone, and רב ששת by carrying beams. רב ששת said: great is work, because it warms the one who does it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף worked at the millstones. רב ששת worked carrying beams. He said: Great is work, because it warms its owner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stays on the subject of beating the cold. It tells how two אמוראים warmed themselves with hard physical work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the cures for chills used food, drink and hot water. Here is another method: hard labor heats the body. רב ששת turns it into a short saying in praise of work.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef busied himself with the millstones.
phrases.notes: Coming right after the chills cures, this means he worked hard to warm up.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet busied himself with beams,
he said: Great is work
for it warms its owner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another way of fighting chills, next to the food cures from step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Physical labor warms the body. גדולה מלאכה שמחממת את בעליה.

steps.title: The ריש גלותא asks why רב ששת will not eat with him
steps.stepSummary: The ריש גלותא asks רב ששת why he does not join his meals.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ריש גלותא said to רב ששת: Why doesn't the master eat with us?
steps.whatsHappening: A new story about the house of the ריש גלותא begins. The question sets up רב ששת's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת had been staying away from the ריש גלותא's table. The question opens the story and gives רב ששת a reason to say what worries him.

keyTerms.meaning: the Exilarch, leader of the Jews in בבל
master, a polite way to address a חכם

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא לְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת:
phrases.english: The Exilarch said to Rav Sheshet:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא סָעֵיד מָר גַּבָּן?
phrases.english: What is the reason the master does not dine with us?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא סָעֵיד מָר גַּבָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story set in the same household as the רב עמרם story.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב ששת avoids eating at the ריש גלותא's table.

steps.title: The servants are suspected about אבר מן החי
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that the servants are not careful. They are suspected of serving meat cut from a live animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Because the servants are not trustworthy. They are suspected about אבר מן החי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the question. His reason is a kashrus worry about the servants, not anything personal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבר מן החי is a limb cut off a live animal, and it is forbidden to eat. רב ששת claims the servants cannot be trusted to avoid it, so their meat is unreliable. The next steps show how he proves this.

keyTerms.meaning: a limb cut from a live animal (forbidden)

phrases.english: He said to him: Because the servants are not of good standing,
for they are suspected regarding a limb from a living animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The servants are suspected of serving אבר מן החי, so רב ששת does not eat their meat.

steps.title: The ריש גלותא doubts the claim
steps.stepSummary: The ריש גלותא asks: Who says that is true?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Who says so?
steps.whatsHappening: The ריש גלותא pushes back and asks for proof. This sets up רב ששת's test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is short, but it works as a challenge. The ריש גלותא will not accept a charge against his household without evidence. Now רב ששת has to show it is true.

keyTerms.meaning: who says? how do you know?

phrases.english: He said to him: Who says so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת's claim from step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's claim that the servants are suspected about אבר מן החי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No evidence has been given, so why should the servants be suspected?

steps.title: רב ששת sets up a test
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת promises to prove it. He secretly sends his attendant to steal one leg of the animal being prepared.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I will show you right now. He said to his attendant: Go steal one leg from the animal and bring it to me.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת starts his proof. Stealing the leg sets up the trap that comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With one leg secretly gone, the servants will be one leg short. If they cover it up by cutting a leg off a live animal, that proves the suspicion.

phrases.english: He said to him: I will show you now.
He said to his attendant:

phrases.aramaic: זִיל גְּנוֹב, אַיְיתִי לִי חֲדָא כַּרְעָא מֵחֵיוְתָא.
phrases.english: Go steal, bring me one leg from the animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 32 by setting up a practical test.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the servants are suspected about אבר מן החי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A test: secretly remove one leg and see how the servants deal with the missing leg.

steps.title: Only three legs reach the table
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת asks the servants to lay out the animal's parts. They bring only three legs, and he asks if the animal had only three legs.
steps.simpleTranslation: He brought it to him. רב ששת said to them: Set out the portions of the animal for me. They brought three legs and placed them before him. He said to them: Did this animal have three legs?
steps.whatsHappening: The trap moves forward. The servants are now caught short one leg.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since one leg was stolen, the servants can bring only three. רב ששת's question puts them on the spot, and the next step shows how they react.

keyTerms.meaning: the limbs or portions of the animal

phrases.english: He brought it to him.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: אַהְדְּמוּ לִי הַדְמֵי דְּחֵיוְתָא.
phrases.english: He said to them: Set out for me the portions of the animal.
phrases.notes: He is now speaking to the ריש גלותא's servants.

phrases.english: They brought three legs and placed them before him.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: הָא בַּעֲלַת שָׁלֹשׁ רַגְלַיִם הֲוַאי?
phrases.english: He said to them: Was this a three-legged animal?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the test that was set up in step 33.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The missing fourth leg puts the servants under pressure to make up the shortfall.

steps.title: Five legs: the proof is complete
steps.stepSummary: The servants cut a leg off a live animal to fill the gap. רב ששת then adds the stolen leg and asks if the animal had five legs.
steps.simpleTranslation: They cut one leg off another animal, brought it and placed it before him. He said to his attendant: Put down that one of yours too. He put it down. רב ששת said to them: Did this animal have five legs?!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of the test. Five legs on the table prove the servants cut a limb off a live animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of admitting a leg was missing, the servants quickly cut one off another animal that was still alive. That is exactly אבר מן החי. With the stolen leg added, five legs show the cover-up beyond doubt, and רב ששת's claim from step 31 is proven.
steps.whatToRemember: רב ששת's test showed the servants would cut a leg off a live animal to hide a shortage. That proved his suspicion about אבר מן החי.

phrases.aramaic: פְּסוּק אַיְיתוֹ חֲדָא מֵעָלְמָא, אוֹתִיבוּ קַמֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: They cut off one from elsewhere, brought it, and placed it before him.
phrases.notes: They cut it off a different animal that was still alive, which is exactly the אבר מן החי worry.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ לְשַׁמָּעֵיהּ: אוֹתְבַיהּ נָמֵי לְהָךְ דִּידָךְ.
phrases.english: He said to his attendant: Place that one of yours down too.
phrases.notes: He means the leg the attendant secretly stole.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹתְבַהּ. אֲמַר לְהוּ: הַאי בַּת חָמֵשׁ רַגְלַיִם הֲוַאי?!
phrases.english: He placed it. He said to them: Was this a five-legged animal?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the test and proves the claim made in step 31.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's claim that the servants are suspected about אבר מן החי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A fifth leg appears, so one must have been cut from a live animal.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The servants are shown to be careless about אבר מן החי, which justifies רב ששת's refusal to eat with them.

steps.title: The ריש גלותא proposes supervised food, and רב ששת agrees
steps.stepSummary: Since the servants cannot be trusted, the ריש גלותא suggests the food be made in front of רב ששת's attendant so רב ששת can eat. רב ששת accepts.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ריש גלותא said to him: If so, let them prepare the food in front of the master's attendant, and let the master eat. רב ששת said to him: Fine, to life!
steps.whatsHappening: The ריש גלותא accepts רב ששת's proof and offers a practical fix. רב ששת happily agrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that the servants were not trustworthy, so the food might include meat from a live animal. The fix is supervision: if רב ששת's own attendant watches the preparation, the food can be trusted. This ends the argument about the servants and moves the story to the meal itself.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, if that is the case
"To life!": a friendly way of saying yes, fine

phrases.english: He said to him: If so,
let them prepare it in front of (the attendant of) the master,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets, so it would just mean the food is made in front of רב ששת himself.

phrases.english: and let him eat.
He said to him: To life!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי הָכִי, לִיעְבְּדוּ קַמֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רב ששת's proof in Step 35 by proposing supervised food preparation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Food made under the watch of a trusted attendant may be eaten.

steps.title: A dangerous piece of meat is served, and רב ששת quietly sets it aside
steps.stepSummary: At the meal the servants put a choking piece of meat in front of רב ששת. He feels it, picks it up, and wraps it in his scarf.
steps.simpleTranslation: They brought a table before them and brought meat before him. They placed in front of him a piece of meat that would choke the eater. He felt it, took it, and wrapped it in his scarf.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues at the meal. The servants try to harm רב ששת with a dangerous piece of meat, and he quietly avoids it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The servants seem to be getting back at רב ששת for exposing them. He does not make a scene. He detects the piece by touch and hides it in his scarf instead of eating it, which sets up the next part of the story.

keyTerms.meaning: A small table for serving food
A slice or piece of meat
He felt it, touched it with his hands

phrases.english: They brought a table before them,
and brought meat before him,
and they placed before him
a piece of meat that chokes the throat.
He felt it and took it,
and wrapped it in his scarf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the meal that was agreed to in Step 36, adding the servants' trick.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ששת avoids the dangerous piece by hiding it instead of eating it.

steps.title: After the meal, the servants speak to the ריש גלותא
steps.stepSummary: Once רב ששת finished eating, the servants turned to the ריש גלותא to say something about him.
steps.simpleTranslation: After he ate, they said to him:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is getting ready for what the servants will tell the ריש גלותא next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The servants noticed that רב ששת did not eat the piece they gave him. They now plan to use this against him in front of the ריש גלותא. Their actual words come in the next part of the text.

phrases.english: After he ate,
they said to him:
phrases.notes: "They" are the servants, and "him" is the ריש גלותא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the meal to the servants' report, setting up their accusation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Transition line that introduces what the servants say next.
